modules.title: 不用鼠标、看不清字的人，也能用你的页面吗

items.title: 图片有文字说明
items.text: 每张有信息量的图片配一段 alt 文字——图片加载失败或读屏时，这段文字顶上。纯装饰的图标可以不给说明文字，但别漏掉有内容的图。

items.title: 键盘能到达
items.text: 拔掉鼠标只用 Tab 走一遍：每个按钮都能到达、焦点位置看得见（Focus 轮廓）、顺序合理。菜单和弹窗打开后焦点要进去，关闭后要回来。

items.title: 对比度足够
items.text: 正文和背景至少 4.5:1。这条同时帮到阳光下看手机的所有人——无障碍做好，普通用户也受益。

modules.title: 它不是什么
modules.text: 无障碍不只是「照顾残障人士」——阳光下看不清屏幕、单手抱娃点手机、鼠标坏了用键盘，都是它覆盖的场景；做好了全员受益。它也不是上线后的补丁：这些检查在开发的时候顺手做就行，上线以后要翻遍每个页面才能补，麻烦得多。

lessonPractice.title: AI 交付了页面，你想快速验证无障碍的底线。下面哪个组合覆盖了最常见的问题？

options.label: 图片有文字说明、按钮能用 Tab 到达、文字对比度足够
options.feedback: 对。这三项分别覆盖看不见图的人、不用鼠标的人和看不清字的人——这三项各管一件事，一起查一遍就能挡住最常见的问题。

options.label: 对比度查过了，页面应该就没问题了
options.feedback: 对比度只照顾「看不清」一种情况；不用鼠标的和用读屏的访客照样可能被挡在门外。

options.label: 只在自己电脑的 Chrome 里点一遍
options.feedback: 同一台设备同一浏览器正是「我这里能用」的陷阱；无障碍要换输入方式和场景测。

en.title: The AI delivered the page and you want to verify the accessibility floor. Which combination covers the most common problems?

options.label: Images have text alternatives, buttons reachable by Tab, text contrast sufficient
options.feedback: Correct. Each of the three blocks one common barrier, and together they are together they catch the most common problems in one pass.

options.label: Contrast is checked, so the page should be fine
options.feedback: Contrast covers only "hard to see"; keyboard and screen-reader users may still be locked out.

options.label: Just click through it in Chrome on your own computer
options.feedback: Same device, same browser is exactly the "works for me" trap; accessibility needs different inputs and contexts.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 交付前自查一遍无障碍：每张图片有 alt 文字说明，所有按钮和链接能用 Tab 键按顺序到达，正文对比度至少 4.5:1。发现哪项不达标直接修，修完列出来。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Run an accessibility self-check before delivery: every image has alt text, all buttons and links are reachable by Tab in order, and body contrast is at least 4.5:1. Fix what fails and list the fixes.

learning.assumes: You have used the Tab key and seen the text shown when an image fails to load.
learning.outcome: You can have the AI self-check against the three high-frequency accessibility checks, and tell them apart from "the page looks fine."

items.title: Images have text alternatives
items.text: Every informative image carries alt text that steps in when the image fails or a reader reads aloud. Purely decorative icons can go without it—just do not skip images with content.

items.title: Keyboard can reach
items.text: Unplug the mouse and Tab through: every button reachable, focus visible (the focus ring), order sensible. Menus and dialogs take focus in and return it on close.

items.title: Contrast suffices
items.text: Body versus background at least 4.5:1. This one also helps everyone squinting at a phone in the sun—good accessibility benefits ordinary users too.

modules.title: What it is not
modules.text: Accessibility is not only "helping people with disabilities"—sunlight glare, holding a baby with one hand, or a broken mouse all fall inside it, and everyone benefits. It is also not a post-launch patch: doing these checks during the build is straightforward; auditing every page after launch takes far more time. The a11y shorthand common in AI replies refers to exactly this.

distinctions.label: Contrast
distinctions.text: {c:contrast} is one specific check—text versus background; {c:accessibility} is the whole effort that check belongs to.

distinctions.label: Focus
distinctions.text: {c:focus} shows where the keyboard cursor is; {c:accessibility} requires it be visible and reachable on every control.

lessonPractice.title: The AI delivered the page and you want to verify the accessibility floor. Which combination covers the most common problems?

options.label: Images have text alternatives, buttons reachable by Tab, text contrast sufficient
options.feedback: Correct. Each of the three blocks one common barrier, and together they are the highest-value floor check.

options.label: Contrast is checked, so the page should be fine
options.feedback: Contrast covers only "hard to see"; keyboard and screen-reader users may still be locked out.

options.label: Just click through it in Chrome on your own computer
options.feedback: Same device, same browser is exactly the "works for me" trap; accessibility needs different inputs and contexts.

lessonAgentPrompt.text: Run an accessibility self-check before delivery: every image has alt text, all buttons and links are reachable by Tab in order, and body contrast is at least 4.5:1. Fix what fails and list the fixes.
